name: grid_3x2
why: Two directions together: three along the 200 edge, two along the 120 one. The full grid is 3x2 = 6 holes, five more than the seed.
_why_the_seed_is_at_the_center: it is a measured thing, not a matter of style. With the seed at (-60, -30) the check DEPENDED on the direction of the edges: the second row fell at y = -60, that is on the edge of the plate, and the three holes came out cut in half. On 10 September 2026 we counted 2 whole holes (2544.7 mm3) plus 3 half holes (1908.5) against the 6361.7 expected: the count matched to the cubic millimetre and the add-in was not to blame. From the centre the grid fits in all four combinations of direction -- x within +-80 out of +-100, y within +-30 out of +-60.
_why_there_are_no_positions: the six centres cannot be written: they depend on the direction of the two edges, which SOLIDWORKS chooses and the case does not know. Here the GRID is measured -- how many holes and how much material -- and the position is pinned by the case `three_holes_pitch_40`, where one of the two coordinates is invariant.
